en: The Chapter on Sandals, 62. The Training Rule on Wearing Shoes.
At that time, the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.
Now at that time, the group-of-six monks were teaching the Dhamma to one who was wearing sandals...
[as before] ... "The training is to be observed: 'I will not teach the Dhamma to one who is not ill and is wearing sandals.
One should not teach the Dhamma to one who is not ill and is wearing sandals.

If one, out of disrespect, teaches the Dhamma to someone who has stepped on [a seat], or who is wearing shoes, or who has removed their footwear, when they are not ill, there is an offense of wrong-doing (dukkaṭa). There is no offense if it was unintentional … [and so forth] …
the second training rule is concluded.
